topic: Physical properties of aldehydes and ketones

Absence Note.Reason: I am at a chemistry teachers' conference today.
Absence Note.Message to class: Keep your NCERT Chemistry book open at page 235. Before each answer, try to rank the boiling points yourself.

Teaching Style.Tone: Clear and curious; connects every property to the forces between molecules
Teaching Style.Pace: Moderate; compares molecules one pair at a time
Teaching Style.Language: Simple, clear English; explains each term (dipole, hydrogen bond, van der Waals forces) once in everyday words
Teaching Style.Habits: Asks which force holds the molecules together before giving any boiling point; uses kitchen and perfume examples

Lecture Structure.Order: Their structures from the book and the carbonyl group, states at room temperature, boiling points and why they sit between hydrocarbons and alcohols, solubility and odour, ranking boiling points with NCERT Example 8.2
Lecture Structure.Must cover: The structures from the book and where the carbonyl group (C=O) sits in an aldehyde and in a ketone; boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than hydrocarbons and ethers but lower than alcohols of similar mass, with the reason for each; the values 273, 281, 322, 329 and 370 K; small aldehydes and ketones dissolve in water through hydrogen bonds; NCERT Example 8.2 and its order
Lecture Structure.Avoid: Chemical reactions such as nucleophilic addition; methods of preparation

Next Class.Topic: Nucleophilic addition reactions of aldehydes and ketones
Next Class.Prep: Read section 8.4 of the NCERT book
